alignments.note: Substantival article takes the pronoun and relative supplied to make the participle a noun, headed on the pronoun one (rule 41).
Participle rendered cometh near; near is a phrasal particle naming nothing on its own, so the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Second article, rendered by the second written relative that (rule 41); the ASV repeats the whole phrase, so nothing here is unrendered.
Second participle, rendered cometh near on the same terms.
Construct noun with the supplied the (rule 29).

The interrogative particle and the following אִם form one interrogative expression for which the ASV writes a single fronted auxiliary shall, so the two share one unit (rules 17, 30), headed on the interrogative. Marking אִם unrepresented beside a הֲ holding shall was the alternative.
תַּמְנוּ is rendered by its subject pronoun we together with the totality expression all of us, headed on all, which carries the lexeme (rules 17, 31); discontinuous around perish under rule 25.
The ASV writes no function word for this preposition before the infinitive, rendering the complement as a bare verb (rules 40, 52).

review_notes: הַאִם is treated as one interrogative expression rendered by the single fronted auxiliary shall; the split reading is named in that unit's note.
all of us realizes the finite verb תַּמְנוּ, since no כֹּל stands in this clause.
